n: Virtual Asset Laundering via Mixers, Tumblers and Chain-Hopping
ds: Criminals obscure the trail of virtual asset proceeds by routing them through mixing services, privacy-enhancing tools and rapid conversions between assets and blockchains. The aim is to break the link between illicit source and final cash-out point. Regulated platforms see this as exposure to mixers, layered swaps and unusually fast pass-through.

src.t: FATF, Virtual Assets: Red Flag Indicators of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (2020)
FATF, Updated Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach to Virtual Assets and Virtual Asset Service Providers (2021)
FinCEN, Advisory on Illicit Activity Involving Convertible Virtual Currency (FIN-2019-A003, 2019)

FinCEN, Proposal of Special Measure Regarding Convertible Virtual Currency Mixing as a Class of Transactions of Primary Money Laundering Concern, Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, 88 FR 72701 (23 Oct 2023)

rat: Mixers, privacy coins and chain-hopping seen at crypto platform deposits and withdrawals; often remote and anonymised access.

ind.n: Deposits with direct or indirect exposure to mixing services
ind.cx: Incoming virtual asset transfers trace to known mixer or tumbler clusters within a small number of hops.
ind.fp: Users of privacy tools for lawful privacy reasons, or exposure via a long, diluted transaction chain.
ind.ds: Incoming virtual asset transfers trace to known mixer or tumbler clusters within a small number of hops.

ind.n: Rapid sequential conversions across many asset types
ind.cx: Funds received are swapped through several tokens or stablecoins in quick succession with no apparent trading rationale before withdrawal.
ind.fp: Active traders, arbitrageurs and market makers.
ind.ds: Funds received are swapped through several tokens or stablecoins in quick succession with no apparent trading rationale before withdrawal.

ind.n: Chain-hopping through bridges shortly after deposit
ind.cx: Assets are deposited, then moved across blockchains via bridges or wrapped tokens within minutes or hours.
ind.fp: Legitimate multi-chain users and liquidity providers.
ind.ds: Virtual assets are moved across chains or bridges and converted soon after being received.
ind.cn: Chain-hopping through bridges shortly after receipt

ind.n: Preference for privacy-enhanced coins with no commercial rationale
ind.cx: Customer converts mainstream assets into anonymity-enhanced coins and withdraws them, or requests such assets despite a simple stated purpose.
ind.fp: Privacy-conscious users; genuine holdings of such assets.
ind.ds: Funds pass through mixers, privacy coins or privacy-preserving pools before or after platform activity without commercial rationale.
ind.cn: Use of mixers, privacy coins or privacy pools around platform activity

ind.n: Withdrawals to many fresh addresses in fixed amounts
ind.cx: Balances are split into many near-identical outputs sent to newly created wallets (peeling or splitting pattern).
ind.ds: Repeated small or fixed-amount transfers to many fresh or new crypto addresses.
ind.cn: Transfers to many newly created crypto addresses

ind.n: Use of anonymising network access to the platform
ind.cx: Sessions originate from Tor, rotating proxies or VPNs inconsistent with declared residence, combined with high-value transfers.
ind.fp: Widespread lawful VPN use for privacy or security.
ind.ds: Sessions originate from Tor, rotating proxies or VPNs inconsistent with declared residence, combined with high-value transfers.

ind.n: Very short holding time between receipt and exit
ind.cx: Account behaves as a pass-through: most inbound value leaves within hours with minimal balance retained.
ind.ds: Funds received into an account are forwarded onward within a very short period, often in near-equal amounts and leaving minimal balance.

ind.n: Cash-out to high-risk or unregistered exchanges
ind.cx: Withdrawals go to addresses attributed to exchanges that lack licensing or effective AML controls.
ind.fp: Attribution errors; unlicensed status may be unknown to user.
ind.ds: Withdrawals or flows go to exchanges or VASPs that lack licensing or effective AML and sanctions controls.
ind.cn: Funds sent to unlicensed or weakly regulated exchanges

ind.n: Customer unable to explain transaction purpose or origin
ind.cx: Explanations for layered transfers are vague, inconsistent or shift when challenged.
ind.fp: Inexperienced users who do not understand the tooling.
ind.ds: When asked about a transaction, the customer gives vague, rehearsed, inconsistent or shifting explanations of its purpose, source or counterparties.
ind.cn: Unable or unwilling to explain transaction purpose or origin

ind.n: Interaction with addresses linked to sanctioned or designated mixers
ind.cx: Transfers touch addresses designated by sanctions authorities or flagged in official advisories.
ind.ds: Transfers touch contracts, pools, relayers or addresses designated by authorities or flagged in advisories.
ind.cn: Interaction with sanctioned or designated contracts, mixers or addresses

ctl.ds: Traces exposure of deposit and withdrawal addresses to illicit clusters and screens wallets with risk-scored alerts. It reveals on-chain exposure.

Screens customers, owners, counterparties, vessels, dealers and addresses against sanctions, enforcement and restricted-party lists at onboarding and ongoing, using fuzzy matching and secondary identifiers. Potential matches are held for adjudication before service or funds are released.

ctl.n: Specialist investigation and suspicious activity reporting
ctl.ds: Trained analysts investigate alerts with typology playbooks, document rationale and file reports where suspicion is formed, with prompt reporting to the competent authority. It converts alerts into actionable intelligence.
Rules that alert on abnormal count, value or speed of movements over defined windows compared with customer profile and peer norms. They provide baseline coverage across many typologies.

Applies additional information gathering, corroboration, monitoring and senior review to relationships or transactions assessed as higher risk, covering purpose, expected activity, ownership and funds. The depth is proportionate to the risk drivers identified.

Briefs front-line, onboarding and investigation staff on current red flags, typologies and escalation routes, including sector-specific patterns and professional-enabler behaviours. It improves recognition of suspicious activity that rules alone cannot see.
Links accounts, devices, addresses, directors and beneficiaries to surface rings, shared attributes and flow structures that single-account views miss. It supports detection of organised networks.
Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.

Detects use of VPN, proxy and anonymising services and compares access geolocation with declared residence and sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions. It reveals concealed location and supports geographic restrictions.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.

ctl.n: Counterparty VASP and platform due diligence
ctl.ds: Assesses the licensing, AML controls, jurisdiction and reputation of counterparty exchanges, over-the-counter desks and other virtual asset service providers before enabling flows, and reviews them periodically. It limits exposure through weak or complicit counterparties.

Collects, validates and transmits required originator and beneficiary information with virtual asset transfers and holds or blocks transfers where counterparty data is missing or unreliable. It brings wire-like transparency to virtual asset payments.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.
